title: The Battle of Manzikert
description: August 1071. The Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan confronts a much larger Byzantine army under the emperor Romanos IV Diogenes in eastern Anatolia. The player commands the Seljuk force, whose mounted archers must exhaust the Byzantine line and exploit the defection of its mercenary wing before the emperor can force a decisive engagement.

issues_found: SALADIN is placed as Sultan Alp Arslan: a Kurdish Ayyubid sultan of the late 12th century standing in for an 11th-century Seljuk Turk. The engine ships no Alp Arslan, so the correct solution was a renamed generic Cavalry Archer or Light Cavalry hero-flagged unit; casting a famous figure from a different dynasty and century is avoidable error.

Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so architecture, unit skins and bonuses are unassigned - the Byzantine keep/monastery and the Seljuk camp may render as anything from Japanese to Mesoamerican.

TREE_PALM_FOREST x8 on the map: Manzikert lies on the high, semi-arid Armenian plateau near Lake Van, not a palm environment. The 'desert riders' line in Romanos' dialogue compounds this misplacement.
Romanos' dialogue calls his troops 'legions' and claims a three-to-one advantage; Byzantine superiority at Manzikert was real but nowhere near that ratio, and the term is five centuries out of date.

The 'Byzantine Reserve Committed' trigger sends reinforcements forward, inverting the actual event: Andronikos Doukas withdrew the reserve from the field, a treachery at least as decisive as the mercenary desertion.

CROSSBOWMAN for Byzantine missile troops in 1071 is an engine-imposed approximation, but the absence of any representation of the Varangian/Frankish (Roussel de Bailleul) or Armenian contingents leaves the Byzantine roster generic.
Objectives text speaks of 'cataphract captains' while the Byzantine roster contains Cavaliers and Champions with no distinguished cataphract unit.
